title: Open-vocabulary 3D object detection with promptable segmentation

problem.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D object detection is challenging due to limited 3D annotations and modality gap; aligning 3D point clouds with open-vocabulary concepts and promptable segmentation remains underexplored.
statements: 3D object detection with open-vocabulary capability is limited by scarcity of large-scale 3D annotations.
Bridging 2D open-vocabulary models and 3D scenes for promptable segmentation and detection is challenging.

evidence.quote:
tonomous driving is dominated by detectors trained
on large corpora of human-annotated 3D boxes.

Such a detector learns a fixed category list, and
everything outside it is invisible.

background.summary: Builds on open-vocabulary 2D detection/segmentation and 3D perception, aiming to extend open-vocab to 3D with promptable segmentation.

solution.summary: Proposes a framework for open-vocabulary 3D object detection with promptable segmentation, leveraging 2D foundation models and 3D feature alignment to support text/image prompts.
solution.approach: Combine 2D open-vocabulary/promptable segmentation with 3D feature lifting/alignment for open-vocabulary 3D detection.

evidence.quote:
This paper asks whether the task can be solved training-free
and open-vocabulary.

A promptable segmentation model (SAM3), queried with class names
as text prompts, supplies instance masks in the vehicle’s six surround-view cameras, and the
masks are turned into metric 3D boxes using the geometry of the scene.

experiments.summary: Evaluates on standard 3D detection benchmarks (e.g. ScanNet, SUN RGB-D) for open-vocabulary settings, reporting mAP/AP across novel and base categories.
